properties.foundation_analysis: Bedrock comprises Carboniferous sedimentary strata (Wardie Shales and sandstone of the Inverclyde Group) capped by glacial till. Facades and monuments utilize local Carboniferous Craigleith and Hailes pale buff-to-grey quartzose sandstone, set in traditional hot-mixed non-hydraulic lime mortar. Basement areas are underlain by well-drained glacial drift over fractured sandstone.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Charlotte Square Gardens canopy is dominated by mature *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime) and *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore), interspersed with *Ulmus glabra* (Wych Elm). Late September phenology shows early senescent canopy chlorosis, partial foliar yellowing, and minor early autumn leaf thinning across upper crowns over mown *Festuca-Agrostis* turf.

properties.architectural_summary: Neoclassical civic square and church (West Register House, formerly St George's Church) terminated by Robert Adam's unified palace-fronted terrace design, completed by Robert Reid. Central church features a tetrastyle Ionic portico supporting a stepped podium, circular peristyle drum, copper dome, and cupola lantern. Flanking terraces comprise 3-storey plus basement and attic ashlar townhouses with rusticated ground floors, projecting pavilion bays with attached colonnades, pitched slate roofs with ashlar chimney stacks, and regular 6-over-6 timber sash-and-case fenestration. Central garden features the equestrian Prince Albert Memorial on a multi-tiered polished granite pedestal.
